text_original: Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer ranks the E 220 d 4Matic T-Modell first with 3,322 of 5,000 points, narrowly ahead of the BMW 520d xDrive Touring (3,294). Reviewer states the air suspension gives a soft ride with high load reserves and very calm motorway running that the BMW 5 Series Touring cannot match. Reviewer calls the E-Class the most engaging of the three, with precise steering, good feedback and strong limit handling, while the BMW pushes wide earlier and lacks front-axle bite. Reviewer praises the E 220 d's economy: 6.0 l/100 km on test versus 6.2 l for the 520d xDrive Touring (WLTP 5.0 vs 5.7 l). Reviewer states the diesel pulls with strong low-end torque (440 Nm) so that it feels like a three-litre diesel. Reviewer states the E 220 d is slower to 100 km/h than the 520d xDrive Touring (8.4 s vs 7.8 s) and lacks eagerness at the top of the rev range. Reviewer states the glass of the cockpit displays does not sit cleanly and rates the BMW's build quality and body structure higher. Reviewer states the E-Class relies on touch operation of its two screens and lacks a rotary controller; it prefers the BMW's rotary-push controller, especially while driving. Reviewer states the lane-keeping and lane-change assistants do not always work reliably and intervene suddenly, more disruptive than helpful, a criticism it applies equally to the BMW. Reviewer states the E-Class T-Modell is noticeably airier in the rear than the BMW 5 Series Touring, whose rear knee room is the tightest of the three despite its greater length. Reviewer states the E-Class has the largest boot in the test (615-1,830 l versus 570-1,700 l for the BMW) plus a larger underfloor compartment. Reviewer states the multicontour seats offer long-distance comfort but feel narrow at the shoulders, while it calls the BMW's optional comfort seats first-class. Reviewer praises the E-Class for a soothing calm in the noise measurements, better than the BMW. Reviewer calls the E-Class the most expensive car in the test (base 69,556 euros, test car 82,009 euros vs 64,350 / 75,930 euros for the BMW) and scores it lower on costs.

Collector paraphrase (not verbatim source text): Reviewer ranks the A6 Avant e-tron quattro second with 3,292 of 5,000 points, narrowly behind the BMW i5 xDrive40 Touring (3,305). Reviewer names the Audi the most efficient car in the test (21.2 vs 23.7 kWh/100 km for the i5 Touring) and the long-distance king with 448 km versus 343 km total range. Reviewer states the Audi has to give way to the BMW in charging performance at the fast charger, despite its higher listed DC peak (270 vs 205 kW). Reviewer praises the Audi's air suspension for comfort on all surfaces, while the BMW's air-sprung rear axle reacts more sensitively to edges and long undulations. Reviewer states the Audi offers good road feel and grip, but the i5 Touring has more mechanical grip and is more agile at the limit. Reviewer states the BMW pulls away from the more powerful Audi in acceleration and top speed (0-100 km/h 5.2 vs 5.4 s; 215 vs 210 km/h). Reviewer states the Audi has the highest share of hard plastic in the test and a less rigid body than its rivals. Reviewer states the Audi's sport seats suit long distances but are less adjustable than the BMW's comfort seats. Reviewer states the Audi's high rear floor forces an unnatural sitting posture in the back, while the BMW's rear seat angle is more comfortable. Reviewer notes the Audi has a practical front storage compartment that the BMW lacks. Reviewer rates the Audi's load area as less usable than the BMW's (502-1,422 l vs 570-1,700 l). Reviewer names the BMW the quietest car in the test; the Audi is louder at 50 km/h (61 vs 58 dB(A)) and level at 100/130 km/h. Reviewer states the Audi has the higher base price (81,450 vs 77,600 EUR) and calls the BMW the cheapest at the checkout, though the Audi's extra cost is limited. Reviewer states the Audi has the lowest running costs, the best depreciation and the best insurance classification in the test.
